column1: # Apple's own list of the 12 blocked eMudhra intermediate certificates, as data: a witness for
# emudhra-2026-10-compromised-keys.pem that is not that file.
# Why this exists. lib/incidents/emudhra-2026-10.json's withdrawnKeys and the fixture PEM beside this file are two
# copies of ONE reading -- the chains the advisory's 12 test hosts served on 31 October 2026. A test that they agree
# therefore proves only that they agree, not that the reading was right. This file is a second, independent source
# for the same twelve certificates, so the test can check the fixture against something other than itself.
# source   https://support.apple.com/en-us/149555  ("About the security content of the eMudhra certificate blocklist")
# source published   2026-10-29 (the page gives no separate last-updated date)
# read     2026-11-01, through the agent's WebFetch, which answers from a summariser rather than the raw page
# What this is and is not. These values came through a summariser, not from raw bytes, which is the weakness INTEL's
# V58 named. So this file is NOT a source anything computes from, and no check derives a key from it: every key in
# the incident file was derived from certificate bytes with LibreSSL 3.3.6, OpenSSL 4.0.3 and node's crypto. Its one
# job is comparison -- if Apple's twelve and our fixture's twelve ever disagree in a fingerprint, a name or an
# issuer, the test says so and a person reads both sources again. A summariser can drop a row or mangle a hex digit;
# it cannot make a wrong value agree with bytes measured three other ways.
# Three tab-separated columns: SHA-256 fingerprint (uppercase, no colons), certificate name, issuer.
